newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU Commission to ponder self-chill can ban.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission to ponder self-chill can ban.

text.p: The European Commission may consider banning self-cooling drinks cans after EU environment ministers urged a probe on Thursday into the possible global warming effects of the cans' refrigerant gas.
Ministers issued a statement noting "with concern reports about the development of self-chilling drinks cans using inter alia HFC-134a which has global warming potential".
They urged the EU executive to investigate how mass-market success of the cans might add to the greenhouse gas effect of better-known gases like carbon dioxide (CO2) from fossil fuels.
The hydrocarbon-based gas, planned for use in drinks cans which are yet to hit the European market, is said to have a far more powerful effect than CO2.
"The Commission will look into this with a view to banning it," spokesman Peter Jorgensen told reporters.
The British newspaper Independent reported that the can, which is said to cool drinks rapidly, had been developed by the California-based Joseph Company.
